learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the secret rules of the three little pointing words that make our English sentences perfect!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We use the article 'An' before words that start with a vowel SOUND (a, e, i, o, u). We say 'an apple', 'an elephant', or 'an umbrella' so the words flow smoothly!
We use the article 'A' before words that start with a consonant SOUND (all the other letters). Like 'a car', 'a dog', or 'a beautiful flower'.
We use 'The' when we are talking about a specific, exact thing, or something that is one-of-a-kind in the whole world! Like 'the Sun', 'the Moon', or 'the boy I met yesterday'.

fun_activity.title: 🍎 The Fruit Bowl Game
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the fruits or vegetables in your kitchen. Point to them and practice saying them out loud with the correct article: 'a banana', 'an onion', 'an orange'!

quick_recap: ⭐ 'A' and 'An' are used when talking about one single, general thing.
⭐ Listen to the starting sound: vowels get 'An', consonants get 'A'.
⭐ 'The' is a special pointing word used for exact, specific, or unique things.
